elements.evidence: Company may terminate the Agreement or any Statement of Work for convenience, in whole or in part.

elements.element: Customer's termination for convenience requires thirty (30) days' advance written notice.
elements.evidence: Company may terminate upon thirty (30) days' advance written notice to Contractor.

elements.element: Upon Customer's termination for convenience, Vendor must provide a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees attributable to the period after termination.
elements.evidence: Contractor must refund prepaid fees for the period after the effective termination date, which substantively provides the required pro-rata refund.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: Contractor may terminate only if no Statement of Work is then outstanding, preventing convenience termination during an active SOW commitment. The supplied Agreement identifies no other fixed committed term.
Company may terminate the Agreement or any Statement of Work for convenience.

elements.element: Customer's termination-for-convenience notice period is at least sixty (60) and no more than ninety (90) days.
elements.evidence: The operative notice period is thirty (30) days, not within the specified 60–90-day fallback range.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee payable by Customer does not exceed three (3) months' fees.
elements.evidence: The clause imposes no early-termination fee, so no fee exceeds the three-month cap.
Contractor may terminate the Agreement for any or no reason.

elements.element: Vendor's termination for convenience may be effective only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: The clause permits termination whenever no Statement of Work is outstanding; it does not require termination to occur only at the end of an Agreement or SOW term. The non-operative margin comment cannot substitute for that restriction.

elements.element: Vendor must give ninety (90) days' notice of termination for convenience.
elements.evidence: Contractor must provide ninety (90) days' advance written notice to Company.

result.reason: The redline satisfies the preferred position by giving Company a 30-day written convenience-termination right, including for an outstanding SOW, requiring a post-termination prepaid-fee refund, and barring Contractor termination while an SOW is outstanding. It does not satisfy the fallback as written because Company's notice is outside the specified 60–90-day range and Contractor's no-outstanding-SOW condition is not an express end-of-term limitation. The drafting is not minimal because it additionally grants partial termination rights and changes Contractor's notice period to 90 days, neither of which is necessary to complete the preferred position. Operative intent is generally preserved, but drafting quality is materially reduced by the unresolved reference to termination only under Paragraph 6, the ambiguity of when no SOW must be outstanding, and the lack of an express end-of-term restriction.
